subject: FQDN canonicalization and CSR aggregation for private deployments

Subject: FQDN mapping / cert distribution requirements for air-gapped private deployment

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. As we start provisioning the on-prem cluster we hit two operational questions your team asked us to confirm:

1) Hostname canonicalization — we are planning to expose a single customer-controlled FQDN per tenant (e.g. app01.acme.prod.local). Acme wants to keep internal service names (k8s service names) unchanged. Do you have a recommended mapping that avoids mass-rewrites (we prefer proxies over host renames)?

2) Certificate trust distribution for air-gapped sites — the security team requires a signed trust bundle and a reproducible process to rotate certs without internet access. We can produce CSRs locally but we need a clear aggregation format and validation checklist so our Ops team can handoff to your CertOps when we have connectivity.

Can you share the minimum artifacts and an example handoff packet (CSR list, desired SANs, CA info, and verification steps)? Patrick also asked if Redwood can provide an ephemeral TLS-proxy pattern so we don't have to distribute root-level CAs into node stores.

Appreciate any templates or a small runbook.

Best,
Patrick

Hi Patrick —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers up front, then a proposed handoff package.

- Hostname mapping: agree with proxying approach. We recommend a canonical FQDN per tenant that resolves to the customer-managed private endpoint. Redwood's runtime supports an internal aliasing layer so k8s service names remain untouched; the proxy performs SNI rewrite and path-based routing.

- Trust distribution: for air-gapped installs we provide a signed trust bundle plus a small "bootstrap CA" artifact (not a root CA) that your Ops can trust locally. You don't need to install Redwood's root in node system stores. Instead, we use a mutual TLS proxy in the DMZ (or an edge bastion) that validates client certs against the bundle. This reduces blast radius for node-level cert changes.

Proposed handoff packet (attached):
- csr_collection_template.csv — fill this with one row per FQDN you want signed (CN, SANs, purpose, requested validity)
- acme_trust_bundle.pem — a PKCS#7-style bundle we will sign for you (for offline installs we'll deliver as PEM)
- delegation-diagram-v1.svg — shows role boundaries and where to place the proxy/bastion

Next steps: please complete the CSV and return. We'll validate and emit a bundle plus a short verification script you can run offline.

I'll loop in Marissa for operations playbook and Karthik for DNS mapping details.

—Olga

Team — forwarding Acme's asks and my reply. Quick plan draft below; please reply with any gaps.

Plan draft:
- Customer will provide csr_collection_template.csv. We validate SANs and minimal CN policy (no wildcard roots unless explicit exception).
- We sign a "bootstrap trust bundle" (acme_trust_bundle.pem) containing: Redwood intermediate + per-tenant leaf certs as required; bundle formatted for both openssl and Windows/Mac import.
- For air-gapped: supply a verification script (verify_bundle.sh) that checks: bundle chain OK, CRL/OCSP stamps (signed assertions), and a test TLS handshake between an offline test client and a pre-signed ephemeral proxy cert.
- DNS: Karthik, recommend we push a short guidance doc for customers: preferred pattern is tenant.example.private -> CNAME -> <redwood-edge> (customer-owned private IP/FQDN). The customer keeps authoritative control over the zone; Redwood only needs the resolution to an IP in their VPC or on-prem edge. We must capture fallback behavior if the CNAME is missing.
- Rotation: recommend 90-day leaf certs by default for private endpoints, rotate via signed bundle exchange window (customer uploads new CSRs; redwood returns signed leaf certs and delta bundle).

Questions for the group:
1) Is a 90-day default OK for on-prem customers with manual rotation? Or should we provide a 1-year default and recommend automation?
2) For the proxy approach, we need a clear list of trust store locations and step-by-step import commands across common distros — Ben can you take that?

Thanks,
Olga

Thanks for the plan draft — a few clarifying points from DNS perspective: 

- Canonicalization pattern: prefer an immutable customer-controlled apex per environment, e.g., acme.app.private rather than per-tenant hostnames scattered across the zone. Then use path-based tenant routing (tenant in path or SNI-based tenant header). That avoids high churn in DNS records.

- CNAME chaining: some on-prem resolvers disallow long CNAME chains; we should make the diagram explicit: customer FQDN -> CNAME -> edge.acme-internal -> A record -> private IP of edge (no more than one CNAME hop).

- Split-horizon note: customers with split-horizon DNS should ensure internal and external zones are consistent for the canonical apex; we should advise a short TTL for the apex so failover to a secondary edge is feasible.

- Validation: we'll add an automated DNS check as part of the verification script that validates the apex resolves to the provided IP and SNI test passes.

On rotation window: 90 days is fine and aligns with best practice. For fully manual kits we can offer 180-day exceptions, but include a mandatory ops checklist (manual rotation runbook).

I'll draft the DNS section and attach to the handoff packet.

—Karthik
